answer: Each claimed identity is bound to a fresh anchor challenge whose response requires a prescribed chain of dependent modular squarings; each result unlocks only the next, so GPUs cannot divide one chain into parallel work. A clone needs its own completed chain, making many identities costly to produce within a deadline, though separate chains can run concurrently. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the voyage efficiently, while time-bound work limits sybil ripple.
